title: Best Places to Celebrate Diwali 2026 in India: From Ayodhya to Goa
summary: Where to celebrate Diwali 2026 in India. Ayodhya Deepotsav with 33 lakh diyas, Golden Temple, Varanasi ghats, Jaipur lights and Goa Narkasur.
body_markdown:
Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8. The full cluster runs from Dhanteras on Friday November 6 through Bhai Dooj on Wednesday November 11. That Sunday alignment means most working people get at least a three-day window without taking leave, and a five or six-day break with just one day off.


But the question is not just when. It is where. Diwali in Ayodhya is a government-organised spectacle involving 33 lakh earthen diyas across the Saryu riverfront. Diwali at the Golden Temple in Amritsar is actually Bandi Chhor Divas, a Sikh celebration that runs continuously for 48 hours. Diwali in Goa involves neighbourhood competitions to build and burn the tallest Narkasur effigy before dawn. Each of these is a structurally different festival experience sharing the same calendar date.


## **Choosing a Diwali Destination by What You Actually Want to See**


The best places to celebrate diwali 2026 depend on whether you want visual spectacle, spiritual depth, cultural immersion, shopping, or a beach-and-festival hybrid. Each city below serves a different version of that answer.


# **Best Places to Celebrate Diwali 2026: What Each City Offers and How to Plan**


The destinations are ordered by the intensity of planning required. Ayodhya and Amritsar need advance booking weeks ahead. Jaipur and Varanasi need a few days’ notice. Goa is the most flexible.


## **Ayodhya: Deepotsav 2026 on the Saryu River**


Ayodhya Deepotsav 2026 runs from November 5 to November 7, with the main lamp-lighting on the evening of November 7, one day before Diwali itself. The 10th edition of Deepotsav is planned with 33 lakh earthen diyas across Ram Ki Paidi and the Saryu riverfront. The 2025 event set a Guinness World Record with 22.23 lakh diyas lit simultaneously.


The lamp-lighting ghats are pass-controlled. The public watches from the Naya Ghat side, the Saryu bridge, and the ghats downstream. Roads into the ghat zone close from the afternoon, and the crowd reaches capacity before the lamps are lit. Plan to arrive at the viewing areas by early afternoon.


A laser and drone show over the river follows the lamp-lighting. Ram Leela performances and cultural programming run across all three days at Ram Katha Park.


The Maharshi Valmiki International Airport at Ayodhya now handles flights from several cities. The city is also connected by rail to Lucknow and by road through the Delhi to Lucknow corridor. Accommodation in Ayodhya fills completely during Deepotsav week. Many visitors stay in Lucknow, about 135 km away, and travel in for the evening.


## **Amritsar: Bandi Chhor Divas at the Golden Temple**


The Sikh celebration of Bandi Chhor Divas coincides with Diwali but carries its own history. It marks the release of Guru Hargobind from Gwalior Fort along with 52 other prisoners. The Golden Temple is illuminated, and the celebration runs continuously for approximately 48 hours.


The fireworks display over the Sarovar is among the most photographed Diwali moments in India. The Harmandir Sahib is open through the night, and the scale of the decoration and lighting transforms the entire complex.


Amritsar in November sits at comfortable temperatures between 12 and 25 degrees Celsius. The city is connected to Delhi by overnight bus, with the[Delhi to Manali bus route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-manali-bus-route) page showing the broader northern corridor options. The Wagah Border ceremony, Jallianwala Bagh and the heritage walk through the old city all fit around the Diwali visit.


Book accommodation at least 2 to 3 weeks before Diwali. Hotels near the Golden Temple fill first.


## **Jaipur: The Pink City Lit From Fort to Bazaar**


Jaipur’s Diwali is visual at a city scale. The Hawa Mahal is illuminated. The Nahargarh Fort lights are visible from across the old city after sunset. Johari Bazaar’s shops are lit with thousands of diyas in the traditional style, and the streets between Hawa Mahal and City Palace carry a density of decoration that few other cities match.


The shopping angle is strong. Johari Bazaar for jewellery and gemstones, Bapu Bazaar for textiles and mojari, and Tripolia Bazaar for brassware and lacquerware all run extended hours during Diwali week. Fireworks displays from rooftop restaurants overlooking the old city are a Jaipur Diwali tradition.


Jaipur is connected to Delhi by bus, roughly 5 to 6 hours. Check current schedules on the[Jaipur bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/jaipur-bus-booking-online) .


## **Varanasi: Two Festivals in One Month**


Varanasi’s Diwali on November 8 lights the ghats along the Ganges with diyas and candles. The nightly Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat is enhanced during the festival. But the more visually distinctive event is Dev Deepawali, celebrated 15 days after Diwali on Kartik Purnima, which falls on November 24 in 2026.


During Dev Deepawali, the entire stretch of ghats from Assi to Rajghat is lined with thousands of diyas, and a separate aarti ceremony runs at Dashashwamedh. Unlike the main aarti which runs nightly, this event is once a year.


A traveller with enough time can plan a trip that covers both Diwali (November 8) and Dev Deepawali (November 24), though this requires a 16-day stay or two separate visits. For a single visit, Dev Deepawali on November 24 is the more distinctive event.


## **Goa: Narkasur Before Dawn**


Goa’s Diwali has a tradition found nowhere else in India. The Narkasur effigy competition runs across neighbourhoods, with communities building towering paper-and-wood effigies of the demon Narakasura. The effigies are burned before dawn on Diwali day, and the scale and creativity of the constructions, particularly in towns like Margao, Ponda and Panaji, is specific to Goa.


November is also the start of Goa’s tourist season. The beaches are cleaned after the monsoon, the shacks reopen, and the water is warm for swimming. Diwali in Goa combines the festival with the start of the beach season in a way no other destination can.


Goa is accessible by flight from most Indian cities, by train to Madgaon or Thivim, or by overnight bus from Mumbai and Pune.


## **Practical Planning for Diwali 2026**


The Sunday alignment means most people have at least Saturday November 7 to Monday November 9 without leave. Taking Tuesday November 10 off extends the window to Bhai Dooj on Wednesday November 11.


For the Ayodhya Deepotsav, arrive by November 6 and plan to watch the lamp-lighting on November 7 evening. For Amritsar, arrive by November 7 to see the full Bandi Chhor Divas cycle. For Jaipur and Varanasi, November 7 arrival gives a full day of shopping or sightseeing before Diwali night. For Goa, the Narkasur burning happens before dawn on November 8.


**Note:** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## **Frequently Asked Questions About Diwali Travel 2026**


### **When is Diwali 2026?**


Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8, with the full cluster running from Dhanteras on November 6 to Bhai Dooj on November 11.


### **Which city is best to celebrate Diwali in India?**


Ayodhya for the Deepotsav spectacle, Amritsar for the Golden Temple illumination, Jaipur for visual city-wide lighting, and Goa for the unique Narkasur tradition.


### **What is Ayodhya Deepotsav?**


Deepotsav is a government-organised lamp-lighting festival on the Saryu riverfront, planned with 33 lakh diyas in 2026 across Ram Ki Paidi.


### **What is Bandi Chhor Divas at the Golden Temple?**


Bandi Chhor Divas is the Sikh celebration coinciding with Diwali, marking Guru Hargobind’s release from Gwalior Fort with a 48-hour illuminated celebration.


### **Is Varanasi good for Diwali?**


Varanasi offers two festival windows: Diwali on November 8 and the more distinctive Dev Deepawali on November 24 with ghats lit from Assi to Rajghat.


### **What is the Narkasur tradition in Goa?**


Neighbourhoods build and burn towering Narakasura effigies before dawn on Diwali day, a tradition unique to Goa with competitive effigy-building across towns.


### **How many days off does Diwali 2026 give?**


The Sunday alignment gives a natural 3-day weekend, extendable to 5 or 6 days with one day of leave on Tuesday November 10.


### **When should I book hotels for Diwali travel?**


Book accommodation at least 2 to 3 weeks before Diwali. Ayodhya and Amritsar fill first due to their specific festival events.


### **Can I visit both Diwali and Dev Deepawali in Varanasi?**


Diwali is November 8 and Dev Deepawali is November 24, requiring either a 16-day stay or two separate visits to Varanasi.


### **What is the best Diwali destination from Delhi?**


Jaipur at 5 to 6 hours by bus is the most accessible. Amritsar and Varanasi are overnight journeys, and Ayodhya connects through Lucknow.
